SALG-01.note: 8x-18=5x+30, x=16. No bound rejects anything without algebra.

SALG-02.note: survivors=2: 4x+6y=9 has same-sign coefficients so its slope is negative by inspection; A and B die on sign. 4/6=2/3 is then near-recall. Frame duplicates SALG-22.

SALG-03.note: roots -6 and 1; greater=1. B is the other root, a real trap. No stem-only bound.

SALG-04.note: survivors=3: -2<x<7 gives integers -1..6 = 8. Stem-only: the x-interval has width 9 (2c/a) so a strict count of 10 is impossible; 7/8/9 all survive.

SALG-05.note: -5x>=18, x<=-3.6, greatest integer -4. B is the wrong-rounding trap. No stem-only bound.

SALG-06.note: rate 16/80=0.20, fee 22, 94=22+0.2p, p=360. Bound check: fee>0 forces p above proportional 94/62*200=303; all four options clear it. Mechanism duplicates SALG-21.

SALG-07.note: Subject-recall shortcut: reflection across the x-axis fixes x-intercepts, so the reflection is decorative; original x-intercept (3/4)x=6, x=8. Not a bound defect, but a student who knows the fact skips the item's named skill.

SALG-08.note: survivors=1: y=x-7, and (1/2)x+(2/3)y=7 with positive weights needs y>0, i.e. x>7. Options 2, -14 and 3 all give y<=0 and LHS<=x/2<=3.5<7. Only 10 survives a one-step sign/magnitude argument. DROP or re-distract with values >7 (e.g. 12, 14, 17).

SALG-09.note: 3p-6q=5q+r, 11q=3p-r. A/C encode forgot-to-distribute (6->1, 7) and sign-of-r errors. No stem-only bound.

SALG-10.note: (3a-7)/(a+1)=2, a=9; check (9,27),(-1,7) slope 20/10. No stem-only bound; sign of a not determinable without computing.

SALG-11.note: Shortcut: extra 168 profit / 2.4 per cupcake = 70 more, 130+70=200; Monday profit and the -180 intercept are never needed. Bound c>130 kills nothing (145 clears). Easy for the stated skill.

SALG-13.note: slope 12/6=2 by inspection, f(3)=c+4=11, c=7. Bound: 11 must lie between c and c+12, i.e. -1<c<11; all four survive. Two lines of work at most.

SALG-14.note: |2x+5|=k+4 has one solution iff k+4=0, k=-4. This IS a recall fact (RHS of an absolute value must be 0), but it is the named skill. A is the x-value trap.

SALG-15.note: s>=2L binding: 12L+10L<=250, L<=11.36, 11. Limiting-thing item by design; the ratio is the binding constraint. Options 15/12 die only by substitution, which does not count. No stem-only bound.

SALG-16.note: survivors=2: 2x-1>=3 gives x>=2, so 3x>=6>5 and y is negative; B and D die on sign. Left with -1 and -19 and the stem says 'greatest', so the pick-the-bigger-option heuristic finishes it. Effectively one survivor. Re-key as 'least possible value' with distractors below -19, or DROP.

SALG-17.note: survivors=3: P=6w+6<=60, w<=9, w=4..9 = 6. Stem-only magnitude: 16 widths would need w=19, L=41, P far above 60; 9 and 5 survive as fencepost/cap errors.

SALG-18.note: f(x)=5 at x=3, so g(5)=6(3)+1=19 (or g(t)=2t+9). C is plug-5-into-composite trap. No stem-only bound.

SALG-19.note: b+9=2(b-4), b=17; check 26=2*13. B is brother's age 4 years ago. No stem-only bound (b>4 kills nothing).

SALG-20.note: x+y=6, x-y=10, x=8, y=-2, xy=-16. Sign argument (x-y>x+y so y<0, xy<0) rejects nothing because all four options are negative. Solve is two lines.

SALG-21.note: survivors=2: 3h+f=88 and 7h+f=192 (144/0.75), 4h=104, h=26. Stem-only: the discounted 144 alone gives 7h+f>=144 so 4h>=56, h>=14 with strict inequality because the discount is real; 10 dies and 14 sits ON the bound (the forgot-the-discount distractor). 23 and 26 survive. Mechanism duplicates SALG-06.

SALG-22.note: 2y-8x=2(y-4x)=2(-3)=-6, one step. No stem-only bound, but the item is a single substitution. Frame duplicates SALG-02.
